identification: Four framed prints. (1) Plate from 'The Quorn Hunt' after Henry Alken (originally Ackermann, 1835): 'The Meet' type scene of hounds and riders, with caption 'Published 1935' on the lower margin, i.e. a 1935 (centenary) reproduction lithograph in a birch-coloured frame. (2) Another Alken Quorn Hunt plate, riders jumping a bank (probably 'Taking a Rasper' style plate), gilt frame with cream mount. (3) A Guinness 'Guinness is good for you' pub-scene print (old man and laughing woman with pints), small timber frame with green mount. (4) A coloured print of a mounted rider on a grey Lipizzaner in Spanish Riding School style uniform, signed in pencil or printed signature at lower right (illegible), in a brown frame with gold slip. All are decorative reproductions, not original 1835 aquatints.

Check the Quorn prints for the 'Published 1935' line (a 1935 lithograph reproduction rather than an 1835 aquatint) and look for foxing or damp behind glass. Guinness print and rider print are common decor items. Reproduction Quorn plates sell A$13-37 each on eBay; the only A$260 sale was an antique engraving and not the same item.
